On Saturday evenings, Tom reviews the notes from class. People around Tom often share different ideas about the work station. Tom thanked Grace for the honest advice. For example, deep work needs uninterrupted hours.
Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. The experience taught Tom more than any book could. Little by little, things began to change. The CEO answers support emails monthly.

The work station looked quieter than usual that evening. The weekly report has become an important part of daily life. Tom prefers snowy weather when running in the park. Best of all, we always keep bottled water in the car.

Grace always says that small steps matter more than big plans. At first, Tom found it difficult to keep the habit. What matters most is not speed, but keeping on. In fact, the bank opened a recruitment drive.
There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. Tom is saving money to buy a ticket to Tokyo. Grace advised Tom to try reading as a new hobby.
